nahhas-irab:1-1.t: الر كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ: that is, "This is a Book which We have sent down to you"; (أنزلناه إليك) is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), as a naʿt (adjective) of (كتاب). لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ: the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and the implied sense is "that he may bring the people out". بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ: (الإذن) "leave/permission" is used figuratively in the sense of "command". إِلى صِراطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: وَما كانَ لَنا أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ: [أَنْ نَأْتِيَكُمْ] is in the position of a nominative as the noun of (كان).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلى ما آذَيْتُمُونا: the intransitive form is أذي يأذى أذى.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خافَ مَقامِي وَخافَ وَعِيدِ: whoever reads it with imāla (inclination of the vowel) intends to indicate that it is from (خفت).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: وَخابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ: it is permissible to put (عنيد) in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: يَتَجَرَّعُهُ: that is, the angels force him to it so that he is tormented by it. وَلا يَكادُ يُسِيغُهُ: that is, [he can hardly make it] go down his throat. وَيَأْتِيهِ الْمَوْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ: that is, there comes to him that from which one dies, from every place of his body. وَمِنْ وَرائِهِ عَذابٌ غَلِيظٌ: it was said: beyond that with which he is tormented there is another, harsh torment.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ: the implied structure according to Sībawayh and al-Akhfash is "and among what is related to you…". Al-Kisāʾī said: [it means] "the likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieved is like ashes". Others said: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); أَعْمالُهُمْ is a badal (substitute) from it, the implied sense being "the likeness of their deeds"; and it is permissible for it to be a second mubtadaʾ, as is related: صفة فلان أنّه أحمر ("So-and-so's description: he is red"). Al-Farrāʾ said: if a reader had read أعمالهم in the genitive it would be permissible, and he recited: [rajaz] 248-
ما للكمال مشيها وئيدا
(What is with the camels, their gait so slow?) «[Translator's note: the source prints «ما للكمال»; the well-known verse reads «ما للجمال» (the camels), which the gloss follows.]»
فِي يَوْمٍ عاصِفٍ: by way of relation (nasab) according to the Basrans, meaning "having storm" (ذي عاصف). Al-Farrāʾ allowed it to mean "on a day whose wind is stormy" (في يوم عاصف الريح), and he also allowed (عاصف) to belong to the wind specifically and then be made to follow (يوم) [in case]. He said: the grammarians have related: هذا جحر ضبّ خرب ("this is a ruined lizard's hole", with (خرب) in the genitive). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is something upon which the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ought not to be construed. Sībawayh mentioned that this is an error on the part of the Arabs, and he took as evidence that when they use the dual they say هذان جحرا ضبّ خربان, because it has become clear through the dual and the singular. A parallel to this error is the saying of al-Nābigha: [kāmil] 249-
أمن آل ميّة رائح أو مغتدي ... عجلان ذا زاد وغير مزوّد
زعم البوارح أنّ رحلتنا غد ... وبذاك خبّرنا الغراب الأسود
(Is it from Mayya's family, departing at evening or setting out at morning, in haste, with provisions or unprovisioned? The ill-omened birds claimed that our journey is tomorrow, and of that the black crow informed us.)
So the like of this is not permissible in speech, nor for any poet we know; how then could it be permissible in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Then al-Farrāʾ recited a verse: [basīṭ] 250-
يا صاح بلّغ ذوي الزّوجات كلّهم ... أن ليس وصل إذا انحلّت عرى الذّنب
(O companion, inform all those who have wives that there is no union once the ties of the tail come undone.)
and he claimed that Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited it to him with «كلّهم» in the genitive. This is something not to be relied on, because the accusative does not spoil the poetry. Whoever reads «في يوم عاصف» without tanwīn [i.e. as a construct] puts the adjective in place of the thing described, i.e. "on the day of a stormy wind".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: اللَّهِ: [in the genitive] as a badal (substitute); and the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you wish, with an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ; and likewise وَوَيْلٌ لِلْكافِرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً: that is, from their graves; and جَمِيعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). تَبَعاً means "having following" (ذي تبع), and it is permissible for it to be the plural of (تابع). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the implied structure is "alike to us are our impatience and our patience".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
إِلَّا أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ: in the position of an accusative, an exception (istithnāʾ) not of the same kind as the first. وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ: with fatḥa on the yāʾ, because the yāʾ of the first person has two usages: fatḥa and sukūn, when no quiescent letter precedes it; but when a quiescent letter precedes it, then fatḥa and nothing else. And whoever gives it kasra is obliged to read هِيَ عَصايَ [Ṭāhā: 18] with kasra on the yāʾ. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read بِمُصْرِخِيَّ إِنِّي with kasra on the yāʾ. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: I have not heard this from any of the Arabs nor from the grammarians. And al-Farrāʾ said:
Perhaps the one who read it this way thought that the bāʾ puts the whole word in the genitive. Abū Jaʿfar said: so this has become, by consensus, impermissible, even though al-Farrāʾ contradicted this and recited: [rajaz] 251-
قال لها هل لك يا تافيّ ... قالت له ما أنت بالمرضيّ
(He said to her: "Would you, O you…?" She said to him: "You are not one to be accepted.")
And the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ought not to be construed on anomalies. The meaning of بِما أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ is "from before", since he had been an associator (of partners with Allah) before them; and it was said: from before the matter.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed "ومثلَ كلمة خبيثة" [in the accusative] by conjunction (nasaq), and they related that in the reading of Ubayy it is: وضرب مثل كلمة خبيثة. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray closing bracket after this quotation.]»

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَأَحَلُّوا قَوْمَهُمْ دارَ الْبَوارِ: two objects.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: جَهَنَّمَ is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (دار). It is not declined fully (a diptote) because it is feminine and definite, derived from their saying ركيّة جهنّام ("a deep well") when it is deep-bottomed.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: (عوجا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is accusative (manṣūb) as a second object, this being one of the verbs that take two objects, one of them through a preposition; the implied sense is "and they seek crookedness for it" (ويبغون بها عوجا).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ: accusative by the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and some call it the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba).
The meaning is that since their affair ended up at this, they were like someone who had done that in order that this might be.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ: concerning يُقِيمُوا the grammarians have several views. Al-Farrāʾ said:
its interpretation is a command. Abū Isḥāq said something like this; he said the meaning is "let them establish the prayer" (ليقيموا الصلاة), then the lām was dropped because the command had already preceded. He said: and it is permissible for it to be indeclinable (mabnī), because the lām was dropped and it was made indeclinable since it carries the meaning of a command. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd related to us from al-Māzinī, who said:
The implied structure is: "Say to those who believe: establish the prayer, [and] they will establish it". This is a good view, because when the believers are commanded something they accept it, so it is the apodosis (jawāb) of the command. وَيُنْفِقُوا is conjoined to it. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خِلالٌ: «لا» is made to have the meaning of (ليس); or, if you wish, you put what follows it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is permissible to put the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative without tanwīn and with tanwīn; and it is permissible to put the first in the accusative without tanwīn and the second in the nominative with tanwīn, or in the accusative with tanwīn. Al-Akhfash said: (خلال) is the plural of (خلّة). And Abū ʿUbayd said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like (القتال), and he recited: [ṭawīl] 252-
ولست بمقليّ الخلال ولا قال
(And I am not one whose friendship is hated, nor one who hates.)

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: دائِبَيْنِ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. constant in what leads to the welfare of people.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
وَآتاكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ ما سَأَلْتُمُوهُ: there are several views about its meaning. The view of al-Farrāʾ is "of everything you asked for", as you say: "I gave him his request" even if he did not ask anything, i.e. what, had he not asked, he would have asked for. «[Translator's note: the Arabic «أي ما لم يسأل لسأله» is elliptical; rendered by sense.]» Al-Akhfash said:
"And He gave you of everything you asked Him something" — [like] أُوتِيَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ [al-Naml: 23], i.e. of everything in her time, something. He said: and it may be by way of multiplicity [i.e. hyperbole]; and Sībawayh related: ما بقي منهم مخبّر ("not one of them remained to give news"), and that is well known in the speech of the Arabs. And there is a fourth view about it, namely that people, in the diversity of their conditions, asked for things, and so they were addressed accordingly.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِناً: two objects. وَاجْنُبْنِي: and by way of intensification one says جنّبني, and one also says أجنبني. أَنْ نَعْبُدَ is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is "from worshipping the idols".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: فَمَنْ تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي: that is, of the people of my religion and of my companions. وَمَنْ عَصانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: that is, to him if he repents.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: رَبَّنا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوادٍ: the object is omitted because «من» indicates it; and likewise رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ: accusative by the lām of kay (lām of purpose). فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and according to most grammarians it is not permissible to conjoin it to what precedes; its parallel is لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ [al-Ḥajj: 5]. And the grammarians recited: [rajaz] 245-
يريد أن يعربه فيعجمه
(He wants to make it clear Arabic, but instead he makes it foreign/obscure.)
Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is permissible in فَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ, taking it to be like لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], i.e. their affair came to this.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ غافِلًا: two objects.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: Abū Isḥāq said: مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُؤُسِهِمْ are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is "for a day on which their eyes stare, hastening (مهطعين)", i.e. rushing. لا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ: [طَرْفُهُمْ is] nominative by (يرتد). وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هَواءٌ is its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
وَأَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا: it is not the answer to the command; rather it is conjoined to (يأتيهم) or resumptive (mustaʾnaf). This has confused some grammarians, to the point that one said: the answer to a command is not put in the accusative with the fāʾ; and this contradicts what al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, and Sībawayh said. The grammarians recited: [rajaz] 253-
يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا ... إلى سليمان فنستريحا
(O she-camel, go at a broad, long-striding pace to Sulaymān, so that we may rest.)
The accusative is ruled out in the verse only because the meaning is not that. أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا أَقْسَمْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ زَوالٍ: that is, of moving away from the respite you are in to retribution and requital.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ: «إن» means «ما» (not); this is related from al-Ḥasan thus, and that like it is فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ [Yūnus: 94], and likewise قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعابِدِينَ [al-Zukhruf: 81]; but other than what he said has been said about these two verses, and that is in their places. Mujāhid read وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال with fatḥa on the lām and the verb in the nominative, and al-Kisāʾī read it so. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, according to what is related from him, preferred the view of Qatāda on it. He said: this is because of their disbelief, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: تَكادُ السَّماواتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ [Maryam: 90]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
Abū Isḥāq held that this came according to the speech of the Arabs, for they say: "Even if you reached such-and-such, you would not attain anything", though one does not reach it; and likewise with «إن». And Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 254-
لئن كنت في جبّ ثمانين قامة ... ورقّيت أسباب السّماء بسلّم
(Even if you were in a well eighty fathoms deep, or were raised up to the ropes of heaven by a ladder…)
And it is related from ʿUmar, ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with them, that they read وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال, with the dāl and the verb in the nominative. The meaning of this is clear, but it is an interpretation and not a reading.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t:
فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ: this is a figurative usage (majāz), as one says: معطي درهم زيدا ("giver of a dirham to Zayd"). And Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 255-
ترى الثّور فيها مدخل الظّلّ رأسه ... وسائره باد إلى الشّمس أجمع
(You see the wild bull in it putting its head into the shade, while the rest of it is entirely exposed to the sun.)

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ: [الْأَرْضُ is] the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ is its khabar (predicate). «[Translator's note: so in the source; غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ is ordinarily parsed as the second object of the passive verb.]» Concerning its meaning there are two views: one is that it will be changed into an earth other than this one, and there are hadiths about this; the other view is that its changing is the removal of its mountains and its being made a level, bare plain, and the changing of the sky is its splitting apart, the scattering of its stars and the folding up of its sun, as one says: "I changed my ring", i.e. I altered it from what it was.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
مُقَرَّنِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). مُقَرَّنِينَ: their hands and feet bound to their necks with chains and fetters. (القرن) with fatḥa on the rāʾ is the rope with which two things are tied together. Jarīr said:
[basīṭ] 256-
وابن اللّبون إذا ما لزّ في قرن
(And the two-year-old camel, when it is tied in a rope [with a stronger one]…)

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
It is permissible for «أن» to be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "with: bring your people out" (بأن أخرج قومك). This is the view of Sībawayh, as one says: أمرته أن قم ("I commanded him: stand"), meaning "I commanded him to stand" (أن يقوم), and then it is construed according to the sense, as the poet said: [kāmil] 246-
وأنا الذي قتلت بكرا بالقنا
(And I am the one who killed Bakr with the spears.)
And it is permissible for «أن» to have no grammatical position, as in أرسلت إليه أن قم ("I sent to him: stand"), meaning "that is, stand" (أي قم); and its parallel is His saying, glorified is He: وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا [Ṣād: 6].

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: هذا بَلاغٌ لِلنَّاسِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. this exhortation has reached them, if they take heed. وَلِيُنْذَرُوا بِهِ: the lām of kay (lām of purpose), and the verb [it depends on] is omitted because the hearer knows it. وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ وَلِيَذَّكَّرَ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ: conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ — and in another place without the wāw. When it is with the wāw, then according to al-Farrāʾ it means "they torment you and they slaughter you", so that the slaughtering is something other than the first torment; and according to others it is permissible for it to be part of the first. When it is without the wāw, it is an explanation of the first and a badal (substitute) from it, as Sībawayh recited: [ṭawīl] 247-
متى تأتنا تلمم بنا في ديارنا ... تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأجّجا
(Whenever you come to us, alighting with us in our abodes, you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ: (إنّ) is given kasra because what comes after the fāʾ in a conditional requital is a fresh start (mustaʾnaf), and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَؤُا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ: as a badal (substitute). (ثمود) is not put in the genitive with tanwīn because it is made a name for the tribe, and it is permissible to put it in the genitive [with tanwīn], making it a name for the clan (al-ḥayy). وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ is in the position of a genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf). لا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: [اللَّهُ is] nominative by the verb. جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ.
And if you wish, you may drop the ḍamma from the sīn [i.e. رُسْلُهُمْ] because of its heaviness. فَرَدُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي أَفْواهِهِمْ: when you use the singular you say (فم), but the original is (فوه), so it is pluralized according to its original form, like (حوض) and (أحواض).
